results.title: Nicol numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Nicol number is a positive integer $n$ that divides $\varphi(n) + \sigma(n)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: $t$-Nicol numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $t$, a $t$-Nicol number is a positive integer $n$ such that $\varphi(n) + \sigma(n) = t n$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function and $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: Every $t$-Nicol number is a Nicol number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $t$ and $n$, if $n$ is a $t$-Nicol number, then $n$ is a Nicol number.

results.title: Fermat unit function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Fermat unit function $u_M$ is the integer-valued arithmetic function with $u_M(l) = 1$ when $l = 2^n - 1$ for some integer $n \ge 1$, and $u_M(l) = 0$ otherwise (in particular $u_M(0) = 0$). Equivalently, $u_M(l) = 1$ exactly when $l \ge 1$ and $l + 1$ is a power of $2$.

results.title: The Fermat unit function at $2^n - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the Fermat unit function $u_M$ satisfies $u_M(2^n - 1) = 1$.

results.title: Small values of the Fermat unit function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Fermat unit function $u_M$ satisfies $u_M(1) = u_M(3) = u_M(7) = u_M(63) = 1$ and $u_M(2) = u_M(9) = 0$.

results.title: Banach–Mazur game theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, player A has a winning strategy in the Banach–Mazur game for $E$ if and only if there are reals $a < b$ such that $(a, b) \setminus E$ is meagre, and player B has a winning strategy in the Banach–Mazur game for $E$ if and only if $E$ is meagre.

results.title: Rayleigh form of an operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Rayleigh form of a vector for an operator `T`: `re ⟪T x, x⟫`. On unit vectors this is the Rayleigh quotient.

results.title: Rayleigh form scales quadratically
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Scaling a vector by a real scalar scales the Rayleigh form by the square of the scalar.

results.title: Eigenbasis expansion of the quadratic form of a self-adjoint operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Expansion of `⟪x, T x⟫` in the orthonormal eigenbasis: a weighted sum of the eigenvalues with weights `‖⟪eᵢ, x⟫‖²`.

results.title: Eigenbasis expansion of the Rayleigh form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Rayleigh form expanded in the orthonormal eigenbasis.

results.title: Span of some eigenvectors is orthogonal to the remaining ones
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A vector in the span of some of the eigenvectors is orthogonal to the remaining eigenvectors.

results.title: Tail of an orthonormal eigenbasis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The tail of the eigenbasis: the eigenvectors with index `≥ k`, as a family indexed by `Fin (n - k)`.

results.title: Head of an orthonormal eigenbasis
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The head of the eigenbasis: the eigenvectors with index `≤ k`, as a family indexed by `Fin (k + 1)`.

results.title: Linear independence of the eigenbasis tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The tail family is linearly independent, as a restriction of the orthonormal eigenbasis.

results.title: Linear independence of the eigenbasis head
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The head family is linearly independent, as a restriction of the orthonormal eigenbasis.

results.title: Dimension of the span of the eigenbasis tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The span of the tail of the eigenbasis has dimension `n - k`.

results.title: Dimension of the span of the eigenbasis head
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The span of the head of the eigenbasis has dimension `k + 1`.

results.title: Upper bound for the Rayleigh form on the eigenbasis tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the span of the tail of the eigenbasis, the Rayleigh form is at most `λₖ * ‖x‖²`.

results.title: Lower bound for the Rayleigh form on the eigenbasis head
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On the span of the head of the eigenbasis, the Rayleigh form is at least `λₖ * ‖x‖²`.

results.title: The k-th eigenvector attains the Rayleigh bound on the tail
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `k`-th eigenvector lies in the tail span, is a unit vector, and attains the Rayleigh value `λₖ`.

results.title: The k-th eigenvector attains the Rayleigh bound on the head
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The `k`-th eigenvector lies in the head span, is a unit vector, and attains the Rayleigh value `λₖ`.

results.title: Courant–Fischer min–max, extremal subspace form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a subspace `W` of dimension `n - k` on which every unit vector has Rayleigh quotient at most `λₖ`, and the bound is attained.

results.title: Courant–Fischer min–max, lower-bound form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every subspace of dimension `n - k` contains a unit vector with Rayleigh quotient at least `λₖ`.

results.title: Courant–Fischer max–min, extremal subspace form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a subspace `U` of dimension `k + 1` on which every unit vector has Rayleigh quotient at least `λₖ`, and the bound is attained.

results.title: Courant–Fischer max–min, lower-bound form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every subspace of dimension `k + 1` contains a unit vector with Rayleigh quotient at most `λₖ`.

results.title: Open unit disc
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The open unit disc $\mathbb{D}$ is the set of complex numbers $z$ with $|z| < 1$, the open ball of radius $1$ about $0$ in $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Injectivity at each parameter of the disc
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc, $E$ a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of complex numbers $w, z$. Condition (a) holds for $E$ and $F$ when, for every $z \in \mathbb{D}$, the map $w \mapsto F(w, z)$ is injective on $E$.

results.title: Holomorphic dependence of a motion on the parameter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mathbb{D}$ be the open unit disc, $E$ a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of complex numbers $w, z$. Condition (b) holds for $E$ and $F$ when, for every $w \in E$, the map $z \mapsto F(w, z)$ is analytic on $\mathbb{D}$.

results.title: Motion equal to the identity at parameter zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a set of complex numbers and $F$ a function assigning a complex number $F(w, z)$ to each pair of complex numbers $w, z$. Condition (c) holds for $E$ and $F$ when $F(w, 0) = w$ for every $w \in E$.

Then $G$ agrees with $F$ on $E$ when $G(w, z) = F(w, z)$ for every $w \in E$ and every $z \in \mathbb{D}$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 109 (the Erdős sumset conjecture)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The upper density of a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is $\limsup_{N \to \infty} \lvert A \cap \{0, \dots, N - 1\} \rvert / N$. This is the statement that every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive upper density contains $B + C = \{b + c \mid b \in B, c \in C\}$ for some infinite sets $B, C \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: $(q, r)$-Dowling polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and let $W(n, k) \in R$ for all natural numbers $n$ and $k$ (intended to be the $(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second kind, but any family is allowed). results.title: Number of comparable pairs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, the number of comparable pairs of $F$ is the number of ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$. It is the number of edges of the comparability graph $G_F$ on $F$, in which two distinct members are adjacent when one contains the other.

results.title: Erdős Problem 777, first question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with $|F| \le (2 - \varepsilon) 2^{n/2}$ has fewer than $2^n$ comparable pairs, that is, ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 777, second question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $c > 0$ there is a real constant $C$ such that for every $n$ and every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at least $c |F|^2$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$), we have $|F| \le C \cdot 2^{n/2}$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 777, third question
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real $\delta > 0$ such that for every $n$, every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with more than $|F|^{2 - \delta}$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$) satisfies $|F| < (2 + \varepsilon)^{n/2}$.

results.title: Shortest common supersequence instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: An instance of SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE is a pair $(R, K)$ of a list $R$ of binary strings (lists of booleans) and a natural number $K$, the length bound.

results.title: Feasible shortest common supersequence instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An instance $(R, K)$ of SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE, a list $R$ of lists of booleans together with a natural number $K$, is feasible when there is a list $w$ of booleans of length at most $K$ such that every list in $R$ is a subsequence of $w$ (its entries occur in $w$ in the same order, not necessarily consecutively).

results.title: The SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE decision problem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE is the decision problem that accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a pair $(R, K)$ of a list $R$ of lists of booleans and a natural number $K$ for which some list of booleans of length at most $K$ has every list in $R$ as a subsequence. Bitstrings that do not decode to such a pair are rejected.

results.title: SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The SHORTEST COMMON SUPERSEQUENCE decision problem over binary strings belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
